newsitem.title: TANZANIA: U.N. tribunal sets dates for Rwandan accused.
newsitem.headline: U.N. tribunal sets dates for Rwandan accused.

text.p: Four prominent Rwandans accused of genocide will appear in court in Tanzania for the first time on February 19 and 20, the U.N. tribunal said on Thursday.
The tribunal from its Arusha headquarters said Theoneste Bagosora, Ferdinand Nahimana, Andre Ntagerura and Anatole Nsengiyumva would make their initial court appearances on those dates.
Bagosora, a former colonel in the Hutu Rwandan army, was widely regarded as the most wanted suspect until he was extradited from jail in Cameroon to Arusha on January 23.

A cabinet director in Rwanda's defence ministry at the time of the 1994 genocide, Bagosora is accused of directing events in the first days of the mass slaughter of some 800,000 people, most of them ethnic Tutsis.

Nsengiyumva is a former lieutenant-colonel. Andre Ntagerura is a former minister of transport and Ferdinand Nahimana is former director of Radio Mille Collines, which fanned ethnic hatred during the killings.
Their initial appearances were announced following release of a U.N. report saying the tribunal was riddled with mismanagement, waste, unqualified personnel and bureaucratic infighting.
The report by Karl Paschke, a German diplomat who heads the U.N. Office of Internal Oversight Services, said not a single administrative area in the tribunal functioned effectively.

Paschke's report, which followed a two-month investigation of the court, was most harsh on abuses in the department of Tribunal Registrar Andronico Adede, a Kenyan, who was cited for spending nearly half his time on official travel.
But Paschke said he was not recommending Adede be dismissed because of the complex tasks he managed to carry out in setting up a new centre with hardly any support from U.N. headquarters.
Adede with Prosecutor Louise Arbor of Canada and Deputy Prosecutor Honore Rakotomanana of Madagascar have been called by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan to New York for talks on February 21.
In Arusha on Thursday, Adede said in a statement it would not be proper for him to comment until returning from New York.
In all 21 people have been indicted by the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, which can impose a maximum sentence of life imprisonment. Eleven suspects are in detention in Arusha.
